S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor occurring within three months of the onset of that stressor. The reaction is considered clinically significant because it is out of proportion to the severity or intensity of the stressor and/or causes marked impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning, but does not meet criteria for another mental disorder. Symptoms typically resolve within six months after the stressor or its consequences have ended, and the course is usually time-limited, though it can become chronic if the stressor is ongoing. It is distinguished from normal stress reactions by the degree of distress and functional impairment, and from other disorders such as Major Depressive Disorder or PTSD by its temporal relationship to the stressor, symptom severity, and absence of a more specific syndromic pattern.

patient.personality: Monroe is a disciplined, detail‑oriented and ambitious worker with a restless curiosity for creative projects, who channels his energy into careful planning, tracking, and hands‑on hobbies.
patient.stressor: About four months ago, Monroe’s routine physical revealed elevated blood pressure and early signs of kidney strain, findings his physician linked to long workdays outdoors, heavy coffee and beer intake, and a family history of cardiovascular disease. The news hit him hard, as it collided with his identity as a disciplined runner in training for a half‑marathon and his plans to advance professionally by taking on more responsibility and coursework in smart‑grid analytics. Over the subsequent weeks, he threw himself into tracking every health metric and expense related to tests and medications, but found that the combination of lifestyle changes, medical follow‑ups, and fears about long‑term complications began to intrude on his job performance, his enjoyment of hobbies like homebrewing and photography, and his dynamics at home. When his supervisor noted his uncharacteristic mistakes on routes and his spouse expressed concern about how consumed he seemed by this health scare, Monroe recognized that his reaction to the diagnosis was disrupting his functioning and agreed to seek psychiatric help.
patient.chief_complaint: “After getting told I’ve got early blood pressure and kidney issues, I feel like I’ve been handling it badly and it’s starting to mess with my work and my life.”

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Ever since the doctor told me about the blood pressure and kidney stuff, it’s like my whole life has turned into a project I’m failing at—I’m constantly checking my numbers, rewriting my running plan, Googling worst‑case scenarios at night, snapping at my wife if she says I’m overdoing it, and then I mess up simple things on my route because my head’s stuck on, ‘What if this means I’m not around in ten years?’
